definitions.text: Brusque ultimatum from union threatening industrial action if wage increase isn't conceded !

parts.words: Brusque ultimatum from union threatening industrial action if wage increase isn't conceded
parts.note: the whole clue describes the curt demand a union makes before a strike: hand over the rise, or face the consequences

explanation.surface: A union delivers a blunt threat of strike action unless a pay claim is met.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a blunt demand for money backed by a threat, exactly the shape of a union's last word before a strike.

clue.text: A speaker who is good at splitting two alternatives

indicators.note: the word at splits the pair of alternatives, sitting between them
two calls for the alternative word to be written twice

parts.note: OR is the word that joins alternatives
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a skilled talker who can divide two choices neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' is the container signal: the speaker's skill seems to be dividing choices, but the word at simply sits between two copies of the alternative word.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplished public speaker is a skilled rhetorician, someone good at addressing an audience.

clue.text: One firm's sword-shaped product .

indicators.note: a product is something made, so these letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the word firm with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A company's blade-like merchandise is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' signals the anagram of ONE FIRMS, the S of 'firm's' counted as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term from Latin ensis, a blade, used of leaves shaped like a sword.

clue.text: Joy and Glenda changing ship

indicators.note: the name Glenda is changing its letter order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A woman named Glenda is moving to another vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' looks like Glenda switching ships, but it signals that her name is rearranged, with the steamship abbreviation added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name happiness or delight.

clue.text: Lost impetus, as the railways did under Beeching

definitions.text: as the railways did under Beeching

explanation.surface: A tale of momentum fading, set against the history of British railways.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Richard Beeching ran British Railways in the 1960s, when lines were cut and steam traction was phased out.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing impetus is the idiom of a locomotive with no pressure left; the railways literally ceased to use steam engines in that era.

clue.text: Rex splits us up to seize power

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Rex splits the words us up by sitting inside them

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Rex, the Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king breaks up a group so he can take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' is the container signal; Rex is the Latin for king, so the surface's king really does take power.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a throne or authority by force or without right.

clue.text: A pound invested in one overseas land or another

indicators.note: to invest is to put money into something, so these letters go inside the land

parts.note: Austria is a foreign country
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Money is being put into one foreign country or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' is the container signal; 'or another' makes the definition simply 'another', a second overseas land.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'another' means another overseas land, and this is a second country.

clue.text: Sort of affront that will soon be upon us

definitions.text: that will soon be upon us

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes an insult of some kind that is approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like 'kind of', but it is the anagram signal for OF AFFRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close in time is imminent, nearly here.

clue.text: Tosti's "Good-bye"

parts.note: Paolo Tosti wrote Italian songs, so his farewell is the Italian word for it

explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Paolo Tosti was an Italian song composer, which points to the Italian farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian farewell, and the title of a song by Tosti.

clue.text: Free of charge?

parts.note: reads as costing nothing, but means relieving a vehicle of its load, or a gun of its charge

explanation.definitionFit: To empty a cargo or remove a charge is to free something of what it carries.

clue.text: Free stabling for Dobbins

parts.note: reads as stabling for horses at no cost, but describes a stall where a horse is left untied

explanation.walkthrough: Dobbin is a traditional name for a farm horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's stall in which it can move about untethered.

clue.text: What one may expect the mineralogist to do?

explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals the anagram of DEAR TO US.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak a statement aloud to listeners is to announce it.
